current_round.prompt:
From: Ethan Jacobson <ethan.jacobson@insurity.com>
Subject: Integration must auto-rebase stale candidates instead of hard-failing on a base/target mismatch

Body:
When a candidate's recorded base_commit is not an ancestor of the candidate, Refine's integration gate hard-fails with Candidate … is stale: recorded base … is not its ancestor and abandons the round — even when the candidate is content-correct and replays onto the current target with no conflicts. This wasted a full round on run 8082 (goal 00000T082ZTBZ3N3EDG591G002): the binding recorded base=a8d44a23 on target_branch=insurity-claims, but the worktree was cut from develop (eacc5984), which had diverged from insurity-claims. The candidate diff was a Claims-only, test-file-only change that rebases cleanly onto either branch.

Fixes required (any one of 1–2 prevents it; 3 makes it self-healing):
1. Single source of truth for the base. Record binding.base_commit as git rev-parse HEAD of the worktree at the moment it is created, not from a separate snapshot of the target branch taken at goal-creation time. This makes the ancestor invariant true by construction.
2. Cut the worktree from the declared target. If target_branch=insurity-claims, create the worktree from insurity-claims (or its recorded base) — not from whatever the main repo happens to have checked out (develop). Today these two disagree; they must be reconciled to one branch.
3. Auto-rebase / replay on staleness instead of failing. When the recorded base isn't an ancestor of the candidate (or the target tip advanced since the worktree was cut), the integration step should replay the candidate's own commits onto the current target tip before failing:
   - base = git merge-base <candidate> <target-tip>
   - git rebase --onto <target-tip> <base> <candidate> (equivalently cherry-pick base..candidate)
   - Proceed with the rebased commit if it applies cleanly; only fail integration on a genuine, unresolvable content conflict — never on a bookkeeping divergence.
4. Replace the strict ancestor gate with a merge-base-driven replay. The strict recorded_base ∈ ancestors(candidate) check is the trigger for the false failure; a merge-base + replay is robust to either side advancing.
5. Re-anchor on automatic retries. A quality/governance retry must re-resolve the current target tip and rebase the prior candidate onto it (or branch from the prior candidate), so a retry can't inherit an already-stale base.
6. Detect the divergence early and loudly. Validate the base↔target invariant at plan/implement start — while the agent context is live and can rebase in-context — instead of only at the terminal integration gate where the sole outcome is failure.

Acceptance: A candidate built on a target tip that has since advanced (or was cut from a divergent-but-clean branch) integrates successfully via auto-rebase; integration fails only on a real merge conflict, with the conflicting paths reported.

governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.

rules.text: Keep component code within `src/{model,process,prompts,surfaces,tools,workflow}` and extend existing architecture instead of inventing new concepts.

## Governance review

Review the exact candidate against the project's stated intent and attached Skills. Read the accepted plans, implementation and Quality evidence and actual diff. Report actual violations with evidence, not hypothetical risks or preferences. Do not edit files, merge, push or change Goal state. A finding must include an actionable recovery request.

## Product intent

Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

## Project rules

- Keep domain concepts, invariants, and pure policy in `src/model`; shared behavior and orchestration in `src/application`; Git, process, host, storage, provider, and telemetry mechanisms in `src/infrastructure`; and adapters for people and machines in `src/surfaces`. Keep `error.rs` as a neutral shared boundary. Model remains independent of the other areas, and code outside Surfaces does not depend on surface adapters.
- Maintain a consistent architecture by extending the existing semantic responsibilities and dependency boundaries described in `docs/intent/01-design.md`. Do not invent new architectural concepts.
- Preserve Rust-based flat-file persistence, file indexes, and in-memory caching. Keep CLI and API work under 50 ms, excluding time spent waiting on LLMs or outside tools.
- Maintain affected documentation, especially `docs/intent/*`, and preserve its established format. Apply the scope limits in the intent guidance below.
- Keep Refine agent-first by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate or reimplement coding-agent functionality.

Update only the affected docs/intent pages when the change alters documented product intent or an architectural contract. Do not require unrelated documentation, cleanup, or broader work.

For this project on the current Default node, /home/buddy/projects/refine-next is the target development checkout and /home/buddy/projects/refine is the serving Refine installation. Use the invocation's pinned workspace (the managed Goal Round worktree when supplied) for code changes and verification, and read the relevant intent from that candidate. Verify paths from the current invocation and runtime before operating on another node. Source promotion and restarting the serving installation are separate operator actions; an ordinary implementation or Quality run should not deploy its candidate or restart the daemon that is supervising it.

## Cohesive code files

Applicability: Apply whenever an agent adds or changes code files in any language.

Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

fetch-goals-from-email.name: Fetch Goals from Email
fetch-goals-from-email.prompt: Fetch new email requests into the selected project's Backlog. This Skill authorizes creation of ordinary Goals from the configured mailbox. Use system.refine_executable to run `system fetch-email-goals --runtime-root <system.runtime_root> --target-root <system.project_root>`, passing each value as a separate, safely quoted argument. This one-shot capability owns secret access, the target-bound sender allowlist, MIME extraction, remote acknowledgement, deterministic Goal IDs, and durable retry records. Do not read or print the mail token, author duplicate Goals yourself, rewrite email source, or modify the request ledger. Inspect the JSON result and report the imported or recovered Goal IDs and any errors. A batch is limited to 25 remote messages; if fetched_count equals batch_limit, fetch another batch, up to ten batches per invocation, then report whether more mail may remain. Stop on a failed command and report the retained retry evidence. Fetching does not approve Goals, change Review decisions, or send email replies. Follow docs/runbooks/development-request-email.md for connection errors.

fetch-goals-from-email-on-startup.name: Fetch Goals from Email on startup
fetch-goals-from-email-on-startup.prompt: Queue the Custom Skill `fetch-goals-from-email` once for this startup occurrence. Run system.refine_executable with arguments `skills trigger fetch-goals-from-email --request-id startup-email-<invocation_id>`, copying invocation_id exactly from this invocation's completion contract. Set REFINE_DAEMON_PORT to the daemon_port parameter for that command. Use safely quoted arguments. Report the queued invocation ID, then complete this startup Skill immediately. Do not wait for the child Skill: releasing this agent slot lets it run even when concurrency is limited to one. Reuse the same request ID if the command needs a retry; do not create a polling loop or fetch email directly. If the target Skill is missing or disabled, report that error without changing its configuration.

release.name: Release
release.prompt: Carry out the release request in the request parameter for the selected project. Use system.project_root as the release repository, system.runtime_root for durable operation state, and system.refine_executable for Refine commands. Read docs/runbooks/semantic-release.md in the project before acting. Use the existing system release-plan, release-prepare, and release-publish capabilities; do not reimplement version selection, candidate integration, tagging, or publication. Always pass the explicit --repo-root and --runtime-root values. Preview the requested semantic increment and report the proposed version and relevant changes. Preparation creates a normal reviewable Goal; retain its operation ID and inspect real Goal and operation evidence. Use the daemon API for asynchronous preparation when useful. Publishing requires the user's explicit publication authorization and an approved preparation; pass --confirm only when that authorization is present. Preserve review and exact-candidate checks. Reuse existing operation IDs for retries and report actual remote tag, release URL, and deployment evidence. Never infer publication success merely from a successful command or local tag.

rounds.prompt:
Recover safely from an old candidate whose recorded base is wrong or whose target has advanced, using the candidate's proven Goal changes.

The original worktree-creation defect was fixed by 8f6de519: fresh and recreated Round branches use the recorded merge-target base. Current code also refreshes candidates before Quality and integration. Keep those behaviors and focus this Round on remaining lineage and retry gaps. settle_stale_candidate still fails immediately when the target equals the recorded base but the candidate does not descend from it. Round 1 retained extensive unfinished replay and publication work without a candidate or final verification.

Validate actual worktree HEAD, recorded base, target and planning or Skill context before automated edits. Preserve the original base when resuming existing work. Extend the current refresh and recovery path to repair bookkeeping only when retained Round and Git evidence identify the Goal's own change range. A merge base or a conflict-free rebase alone does not prove that every commit on a divergent developer branch belongs to the Goal. Ambiguous or unavailable history must remain recoverable with clear evidence, not import unrelated work.

Replay an unambiguous candidate onto one observed target tip in a managed workspace. Record original and replacement identities, retain the source attempt, and rerun the applicable current Skills and exact-candidate checks for every changed candidate. Respect required, background and context-only behavior and record when no required check Skills apply. Bound retries for target movement, preserve conflict evidence and existing supported conflict recovery, and never treat dirty work, lost authority or a Git error as a successful replay.

Preserve target leases and atomic publication checks against the previously recorded remote candidate SHA. Handle an already-published identical replacement idempotently; preserve unexpected remote changes and interrupted publication evidence.

Verify advanced targets, a wrong recorded base with an unchanged target, divergent branches containing unrelated commits, retries, content conflicts, remote publication races and interruption. Prove fresh Round creation still starts at the declared target and that replacement commits cannot reuse stale check evidence.

This is a recovery Round following the Skills review on 10 September 2026. Start from current main in a new managed Round worktree. Preserve Round 1, its plans, logs, branches, commits and uncommitted files; inspect and selectively reuse useful work instead of replaying the whole old attempt. Use the current Skills and docs/intent contracts, not archived Governance, Quality or Guidance configuration or the old fixed planning sequence. Refine owns workflow advancement and integration; human approval remains separate. Update only affected documentation and report focused verification with actual results.
